findings.reason: the node would need one added planted group carrying an unbeatable rate, plus the run that shows it reported and not cut, which is a section change.
findings.text: §5 ("Each further group follows in the ruled order") has no planted control: its only failure-shaped measure is conditional on a real group failing the bar within a "spend the lead rules for it", so if every further group happens to pass, the "reported with its measured rate and the classes that hold it, and is not cut" arm never runs, and the section cannot show its refusal fires; §3 and §4 both plant the fault they need to see refused

findings.reason: splitting the comparison from the cut, or naming which of the two closes §4, changes the node plan a later node is dispatched against.
findings.text: §4's done-when closes on two independent verdicts: "the repair comparison reports, per arm, the members the second reading finds repaired, still defective and made worse ... and says which arm did better", and "the group then meets the bar of §3 on the second reading and its release candidate is cut to the fork"; either can pass while the other fails (the arm comparison can be decidable while the group misses the bar, and the group can reach the bar with no arm difference), and neither is named as the node's one goal

findings.reason: §4 needs a stated route (withdraw, backfill, or a lead ruling recorded as an exception the bar reads) for a sourceless member, otherwise the first group can never be cut and a node discovers it only after the full audit and both repairs are spent.
findings.text: §3's bar refuses the cut "when any member has no source", but §4's done-when supplies clearing routes only for defects the audit assigns to a repair, for duplicates and wrong domains, and for members it "lists by name"; a member that is sound on every class of §1 and has no source is refused by the bar and has no route back to it, so §4's assertion that "the group then meets the bar of §3" is not reachable by anything the plan states; §2's own census (3,205 of 3,266 names "record the domains of their sources", leaving 61 unrecorded) shows such members are present and were not excluded from the first group's membership
